name: Santa Rosa Street Railway (horse cars): Fourth Street and McDonald Avenue
note: Horse-car line along Fourth Street from the railroad depot and out McDonald Avenue, drawn on Thos. H. Thompson's Map of the City of Santa Rosa of 1876 (Historical Atlas of Sonoma County, 1877): in service by 1877 (start ESTIMATED from the map). The Santa Rosa horse lines were consolidated into the Petaluma & Santa Rosa Railway on 20 June 1903 and replaced by its electric cars, downtown from 1 March 1905 (Wikipedia, Petaluma and Santa Rosa Railroad). Geometry: OHM, from the 1876 map. https://www.openhistoricalmap.org/way/198305780 https://www.openhistoricalmap.org/way/198305783

name: Petaluma & Santa Rosa electric cars on Fourth Street (Santa Rosa)
note: The interurban reached downtown Santa Rosa when its crossing of the steam railroad was installed on 1 March 1905; 'the Santa Rosa line was dismantled from McDonald Avenue to Olive Street in 1931' (Wikipedia; month ESTIMATED). Fourth Street between the depot and McDonald Avenue is drawn; the approach from Sebastopol Avenue is not. Geometry: OHM (the horse-car line of the 1876 map). https://www.openhistoricalmap.org/way/198305780

name: Train ferry: Port Costa - Benicia (Solano, Contra Costa)
note: Central Pacific train ferry Solano (from Dec 1879; Contra Costa from 1914) across the Carquinez Strait until the Martinez-Benicia rail bridge opened 15 Oct 1930. Geometry: OHM (USGS Karquines 1898 sheet) https://www.openhistoricalmap.org/way/200461193
